{{2025–26 Big 12 men's basketball standings}}
The '''2025–26 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Cincinnati]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Bearcats, led by fifth-year head coach [[Wes Miller]], played their home games at [[Fifth Third Arena]] in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]] as third-year members of the [[Big 12 Conference]].

== Previous season ==
{{main|2024–25 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team}}

The Bearcats finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|season]] 19–16 and 7–13 in [[2024–25 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 play]] to finish in tie for 12th place in the conference standings, thus earning the 13th seed in the [[2025 Big 12 men's basketball tournament]].  They defeated [[2024–25 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team|Oklahoma State]] in the first round before losing to [[2024–25 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]] in the second round.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reed, Mitchell Power Men’s Hoops Past Oklahoma State in Big 12 First Round |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2025/03/11/reed-mitchell-power-mens-hoops-past-oklahoma-state-in-big-12-first-round}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Men’s Hoops Falls to Iowa State in Big 12 Championship Second Round |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2025/03/12/mens-hoops-falls-to-iowa-state-in-big-12-championship-second-round}}</ref>

The Bearcats were invited to play in inaugural [[2025 College Basketball Crown|College Basketball Crown]], a [[Single-elimination tournament|single-elimination]], fully-[[Bracket (tournament)|bracket]]ed men's college basketball postseason tournament featuring sixteen [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] teams not selected to participate in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What is the College Basketball Crown: Everything to know about the postseason tournament on Fox |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-basketball/college-basketball-crown-fox-everything-know-about-postseason-tournament |date=March 6, 2025 |website=FoxSports.com |access-date=12 March 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://collegebasketballcrown.com/ |title=College Basketball Crown |access-date=March 12, 2025}}</ref> In their first round game, they defeated [[2024–25 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] and lost to fellow Big 12 Conference opponent [[2024–25 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF]] in their quarterfinals game, 88–80.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bearcats Roll DePaul, 83-61, in College Basketball Crown Opener |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2025/04/1/bearcats-roll-depaul-83-61-in-college-basketball-crown-opener}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cincinnati Falls to UCF in Las Vegas |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2025/04/3/cincinnati-falls-to-ucf-in-las-vegas}}</ref>

== Offseason ==
===Coaching staff changes===
Former assistant coach Drew Adams accepted an assistant coach job with [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], following two years at Cincinnati.<ref>{{cite web |title=Drew Adams Officially Added To Indiana Men’s Basketball Coaching Staff |url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/basketball/drew-adams-officially-added-to-indiana-men-s-basketball-coaching-staff-01jwbvqs5tg6}}</ref>  [[Mamadou N'Diaye (basketball, born 1975)|Mamadou N'Diaye]] accepted the assistant coaching vacancy after spending the previous four seasons at [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mamadou N'Diaye Assistant Coach |url=https://gobearcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/season/2025-26/staff/mamadou-ndiaye}}</ref>

=== Departures ===
Any players who have declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]]—including seniors, who must opt into this year's draft—have the option to return if they make a timely withdrawal from the draft and end any pre-draft relationships with [[sports agent|agents]]. Thus, separate lists will initially be maintained for confirmed and potential departures.
